questions.questionText: Express 0.333... (3 recurring) as a fraction.
questions.shortcut: Single recurring digit d gives d/9.

questions.questionText: Express 0.4545... (45 recurring) as a fraction in lowest terms.
questions.explanation: A two-digit block repeating gives 45/99. Divide numerator and denominator by 9: 0.(45) = 45/99 = 5/11.
questions.shortcut: Two recurring digits ab give ab/99.

questions.questionText: Which of the following fractions has a terminating decimal expansion?
questions.explanation: 7/40 has denominator 2³ × 5, which contains only 2 and 5, so it terminates (0.175). The other denominators 12, 15, 30 contain the factor 3.
questions.shortcut: Denominator with only 2s and 5s ⇒ terminating.

questions.questionText: What is the value of 0.777... + 0.222...?
questions.shortcut: Add the fractions d/9.

questions.questionText: What is the length of the repeating block in the decimal expansion of 1/7?
questions.explanation: Divide 1 by 7: 1/7 = 0.142857 142857... The remainders cycle through 1, 3, 2, 6, 4, 5. So the repeating block 142857 has 6 digits.
questions.shortcut: For prime p, period divides p − 1; 1/7 has the full period 6.

questions.questionText: Which of the following decimals is rational?
questions.explanation: 0.1313... is a recurring decimal equal to 13/99, so it is rational. The other three are non-terminating, non-repeating (or the root of a non-square), hence irrational.
questions.shortcut: Recurring or terminating ⇒ rational.

questions.questionText: Convert 5/16 into a decimal.
questions.shortcut: Multiply numerator and denominator to make the denominator 10ⁿ.

questions.questionText: Express 0.1232323... (that is, 0.1(23) with 23 recurring) as a fraction in lowest terms.
questions.shortcut: Mixed recurring: (all digits − non-repeating digits) / (9s for repeating then 0s for non-repeating).

questions.questionText: Express 2.363636... (36 recurring) as an improper fraction.
questions.shortcut: Whole part + ab/99.

questions.questionText: What is 0.2727... + 0.3636... as a fraction in lowest terms?
questions.shortcut: Add the numerators over 99.

questions.questionText: What is the 50th digit after the decimal point in the expansion of 3/7?
questions.explanation: 3/7 = 0.428571 428571... with block length 6. 50 = 6 × 8 + 2, so the 50th digit is the 2nd digit of the block: 2.
questions.shortcut: Position mod block length.

questions.questionText: 1/13 = 0.076923 076923... What is the sum of the digits in one repeating block?
questions.shortcut: Add the six digits of the block.

questions.questionText: What is the length of the repeating block in the decimal expansion of 1/17?
questions.explanation: The order of 10 modulo 17 is 16 (10 is a primitive root mod 17), so the block has 16 digits.
questions.shortcut: Period = order of 10 modulo the denominator.

questions.questionText: For how many integers n from 1 to 60 does n/60 have a terminating decimal expansion?
questions.explanation: 60 = 2² × 3 × 5. The fraction terminates only if the factor 3 cancels, i.e. n is a multiple of 3. Multiples of 3 from 1 to 60: 20.
questions.shortcut: The unwanted prime must cancel.

questions.questionText: What is the length of the repeating block in the decimal expansion of 1/27?
questions.explanation: 1/27 = 0.037037..., so the block 037 repeats with length 3.
questions.shortcut: 27 divides 999.

questions.questionText: What is 0.6666... − 0.4444... as a fraction?
questions.shortcut: Subtract d/9 forms directly.

questions.questionText: What is the value of 142857 × 7?
questions.explanation: 142857 is the repeating block of 1/7, so 142857 × 7 = 999999.

questions.questionText: How many positive integers d not exceeding 50 are there for which 1/d has a terminating decimal expansion?
questions.explanation: d must be of the form 2ᵃ5ᵇ: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 16, 20, 25, 32, 40, 50. That is 12 values.
questions.shortcut: List numbers made only of 2s and 5s.

questions.questionText: If 5/33 = 0.ababab... (ab recurring), what is a + b?
questions.shortcut: Convert the denominator to 99.

questions.questionText: The decimal expansion of 1/7 is 0.142857 142857... What is the 100th digit after the decimal point?
questions.explanation: The block length is 6. 100 = 6 × 16 + 4, so the 100th digit is the 4th digit of the block 142857, which is 8.
questions.shortcut: Position mod 6.

questions.questionText: Which of the following fractions has a non-terminating recurring decimal expansion?
questions.explanation: 60 = 2² × 3 × 5; 13 is not divisible by 3, so the factor 3 remains in the denominator and the decimal recurs. 80 = 2⁴ × 5, 125 = 5³ and 250 = 2 × 5³ all terminate.
questions.shortcut: Reduce the fraction first, then inspect the denominator.

questions.questionText: What is the value of 0.111... + 0.0111... + 0.00111... (each with 1 recurring) as a fraction in lowest terms?
questions.shortcut: Each term is the previous one divided by 10.

questions.questionText: What is the sum of the first 100 digits after the decimal point in the expansion of 1/7?
questions.explanation: Each block 142857 has digit sum 27. 100 = 6 × 16 + 4. Sixteen full blocks give 16 × 27 = 432; the next four digits 1, 4, 2, 8 add 15. Total = 447.
questions.shortcut: Full blocks × block sum + leftover digits.

questions.questionText: If x = 0.1(23), that is 0.1232323... with 23 recurring, what is 1/x as a fraction in lowest terms?
questions.shortcut: Convert to a fraction first, then invert.

questions.questionText: For how many integers n from 1 to 210 does n/210 have a terminating decimal expansion?
questions.explanation: 210 = 2 × 3 × 5 × 7. The primes 3 and 7 must cancel, so n must be a multiple of 21. Multiples of 21 up to 210: 10.
questions.shortcut: Cancel every prime other than 2 and 5.
